dial.summary: BTC Accumulation thesis intact on Aug 30 with 7 of 8 indicators supportive: Global M2 at $103.4T rising on a 4-week basis, ISM PMI at 55.6% (August print drops Sep 1), real yields falling at 2.34%, 2s10s steepening to +39bps, and stablecoin dominance declining to 11.26% with BTC.D holding at 57.4%—DXY at 99.68 remains in the neutral band and sliding, maintaining a constructive backdrop for risk assets heading into the Sep 1 ISM / Sep 4 NFP / Sep 10 ECB / Sep 11 CPI data cluster before FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; ~6-week reporting lag on full aggregate); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (record high, +$102.8B MoM, 29th consecutive monthly increase, +6.11% YoY, per BEA Aug 29 release); global M2 rising ~$0.7T over 4 weeks from ~$102.7T (late June 2026) to $103.4T (July 2026); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; 4-week uptrend confirmed; August global aggregate not yet available (6-week lag); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); September FOMC (Sep 16) is the next key catalyst for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading—August 2026 data releases tomorrow, September 1 at 10:00 AM ET; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8%, Prices Paid 71.1%; highest reading since May 2022; 4-week trend up (June 53.3% → July 55.6%, +2.3pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met); a September 1 reading below 50 alongside any hawkish policy signal would trigger a Risk Off reassessment ahead of FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.68 on August 30, 2026 (up 0.08% on the day; Aug 28 Friday close was ~99.67; markets were closed Aug 29 Saturday, this is the most recent tradeable level); 4-week trend down: DXY peaked near 100.8–101.0 in late July 2026 and has declined to 99.68, a ~1.1% decline over 4 weeks, above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury buyback program and rate-cut expectations ahead of FOMC Sep 16; status neutral (ICE DXY at 99.68 within 97.5–100 neutral band); Sep 1 ISM and Sep 4 NFP are next decisive inputs—a dovish macro outcome cluster accelerates DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive territory).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.34% as of August 26, 2026 (H.15; no new data Aug 29–30 weekend); 4-week trend down: ~2.43% (July 25, 2026) → 2.34% (Aug 26) = −9bps, a confirmed falling trend; status supportive (falling trend satisfies the supportive condition per rule); the headwind rule requires both rising AND above 2%—the above-2% criterion is met, but the falling trend dominates status scoring; inflation (PCE) at 3.7% YoY (July 2026, released Aug 26) maintains elevated real yields in absolute terms, but the 4-week downtrend is the operative status driver; Sep 11 CPI and Sep 16 FOMC rate decision are the next key compression catalysts.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 28, 2026 H.15 close: 10Y yield 4.73%, 2Y yield 4.34% (per etfdb Treasury Yields Snapshot Aug 28); spread = +39bps (+0.39%); markets closed Aug 29–30 weekend, data unchanged from Friday close; 4-week steepening: ~+35bps (late July 2026) → +39bps (Aug 28) = +4bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening direction intact); upcoming catalysts: NFP (Sep 4), ECB (Sep 10), CPI (Sep 11), and FOMC (Sep 16) are the next curve-shaping inputs.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,730,912M (~$6.73T) for week ending August 26, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27); unchanged from prior run; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (late July / early August) → $6.73T (Aug 26) = ~+$31B (+0.5%), within the flat threshold; minor week-over-week dip from $6.745T (Aug 19) to $6.731T (Aug 26) = −$14B reflects routine measured QT operations; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal and no overnight rate spike; status supportive (holding flat; QT pace stable).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate held at approximately −0.0048% (MacroMicro aggregate; prior observation Aug 28, 2026); CoinGlass, coinalyze, and bitcoinmagazinepro all blocked by egress proxy this run—value unchanged from prior run per sourcing rules; search evidence suggests funding has shifted to slightly positive territory across exchanges as of Aug 29–30 (BTC at ~$77,844, down from $80,294 Aug 28 post-Warsh Jackson Hole), but no specific verified percentage is available; funding remains well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold based on all available signals; 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August; status supportive (near-zero funding, no long-side overextension signal). (Value held from prior run; BTC Funding Rates flagged as skipped this cycle—CoinGlass proxy-blocked.)

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (CoinGecko Aug 30, 2026); total crypto market cap $2.71T; stablecoin dominance 11.26% (updated from 10.91% Aug 29—day-over-day tick up reflects BTC spot decline dragging total crypto cap, not capital rotation into stablecoins); BTC.D 57.42% (firm, above 55% alt-rotation trigger threshold; BTC at ~$77,844 on Aug 29); 30-day trend down: confirmed—from ~13–14% in late July 2026 to 11.26% today; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL also rises—does not apply as total crypto cap is down on the day); BTC.D holding above 55% keeps Alt Rotation signal un-triggered.

upcoming.title: Chicago PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Chicago Business Barometer for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET—released the last business day of August (Monday August 31, tomorrow); regional manufacturing cross-check ahead of the September 1 national ISM Manufacturing PMI release; a reading above 50 reinforces broad manufacturing expansion; a collapse below 50 would add downside risk into the ISM print and FOMC Sep 16 positioning.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Manufacturing PMI Report on Business at 10:00 AM ET—first post-Jackson Hole activity read; July 2026 ISM at 55.6% (highest since May 2022); a sustained expansion above 50 reinforces risk asset positioning; a collapse below 50 alongside any hawkish signal would trigger a Risk Off reassessment ahead of FOMC September 16.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP releases the August 2026 National Employment Report at 8:15 AM ET—private sector employment proxy arriving two days before the official NFP (September 4); July ADP showed +44,000 private-sector jobs; a second weak reading reinforces the July NFP shock (−23K) and bolsters the rate-cut case heading into FOMC Sep 16; a strong rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Non-Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET—services sector counterpart to manufacturing ISM; services represent ~80% of US GDP; released one business day ahead of the August NFP report (September 4); a post-Jackson Hole services expansion reinforces the soft-landing narrative ahead of FOMC September 16.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 29, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 29—first post-Jackson Hole labor read; sets early framing ahead of the August NFP report (September 4) and FOMC September 16; a spike above 220K reinforces the case for a cut; a stable-to-declining read keeps the policy debate open heading into NFP.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the second-to-last major data point before FOMC September 16 (after CPI Sep 11); July 2026 NFP shocked at −23K (vs +79K forecast), ADP July +44K; a further contraction would strongly argue for a rate cut and likely push DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive for risk assets); a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; NFP and CPI Sep 11 form the final data trifecta shaping the September FOMC decision.
